#### What this PR does / why we need it:

With [Hostprocess CRI](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/99576/commits/51a02fdb80cb7ba042a66362eb76facd2fd82401) updates the podsandbox was passed RunAsUserName to the security context in CRI and containerd (1.6+) was updated to use the CRI sandbox info: https://github.com/containerd/containerd/pull/5865.

This puts the pod into pending state which is expected: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/104635#issuecomment-910415666

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

-->
Fixes #104635 

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

It was decided to fix the test now, and create a new feature request to add additional information to pod sandbox failures to mark them in failed if the runtime knows it can: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/104635#issuecomment-910499439

issue_context.title: Pods that fail to create podsandbox due to errors don't mark the pods as failed
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please only use this template for submitting reports about continuously failing tests or jobs in Kubernetes CI -->

#### Which jobs are failing:
ci-kubernetes-e2e-aks-engine-azure-master-windows-containerd-nightly

#### Which test(s) are failing:

Kubernetes e2e suite.[sig-windows] [Feature:Windows] SecurityContext should not be able to create pods with unknown usernames

#### Since when has it been failing:

August 26th 2021

#### Testgrid link:

https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-windows-master-release#aks-engine-windows-containerd-nightly

https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-jenkins/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-aks-engine-azure-master-windows-containerd-nightly/1431067557489545216

#### Reason for failure:

```
Successfully assigned windows-run-as-username-204/run-as-username-360fe1a2-16b6-466c-afff-bb455abee8a3 to 1960k8s000
Aug 27 02:10:37.987: INFO: At 2021-08-27 02:05:44 +0000 UTC - event for run-as-username-360fe1a2-16b6-466c-afff-bb455abee8a3: {kubelet 1960k8s000} FailedCreatePodSandBox: Failed to create pod sandbox: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to start sandbox container task "451a4ea594e6bca9c55f96f1ad9481eff768598c9d9e53f23264ccafa729db92": hcs::System::CreateProcess 
```

#### Anything else we need to know:

This runs the nightly builds of containerd and this broke after https://github.com/containerd/containerd/pull/5865

It looks like the pod stays in `pending` phase even though the pod sandbox has failed:

```
Aug 27 02:10:35.933: INFO: Pod "run-as-username-360fe1a2-16b6-466c-afff-bb455abee8a3": Phase="Pending", Reason="", readiness=false. Elapsed: 4m59.111453568s
Aug 27 02:10:37.934: FAIL: Unexpected error:
    <*errors.errorString | 0xc0069f4c10>: {
        s: "Gave up after waiting 5m0s for pod \"run-as-username-360fe1a2-16b6-466c-afff-bb455abee8a3\" to be \"terminated due to deadline exceeded\"",
    }
    Gave up after waiting 5m0s for pod "run-as-username-360fe1a2-16b6-466c-afff-bb455abee8a3" to be "terminated due to deadline exceeded"
occurred
```

This looks to happen because the pod phase is calculated on the containers not related to sandbox containers:  https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/fca3175df7a453c24eec3c11b632090c49472c9d/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L1310

#### Question
Should pods be marked failed if the sandbox pods fail or should we be updating our test to check for the correct failure (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/fca3175df7a453c24eec3c11b632090c49472c9d/test/e2e/windows/security_context.go#L51)

/sig windows
/sig test

@marosset, as discussed at [sig node meeting yesterday](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Ne57gvidMEWXR70OxxnRkYquAoMpt56o75oZtg-OeBg/edit#bookmark=id.vierpxci16cl), this is expected behavior. Do you plan to adjust the test? Or what would be the next steps?

Relevant discussion notes:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/104635 
[Derek] PodPhases are designed this way and the hope is that sandbox will be created. It is hard to change this behavior/assumption
[Alex] should we have a condition or known errors which will indicate the terminate state?
[Ibrahim] another example - image that doesn’t match the platform will never start
[] CSI failure is another example where kubelet keep retrying even if the failure is terminal
[Derek] maybe look into the timeout when kubelet should stop trying to start the pod and will mark is failed?
There is also a device plugin scenario where pod cannot be scheduled on the node
[Derek] if this were only CRI flows, it would be easier
[rphillips] found a link after the meeting, there is a logic to recreate a sandbox if it failed, perhaps the error is not being reported in the sandbox statuses [link](https://github.com/rphillips/kubernetes/blob/d1da6d47dd9dc8eeee9b96bffa9523e4c91f32b8/pkg/kubelet/kuberuntime/kuberuntime_manager.go#L482-L516)

Thanks @SergeyKanzhelev 

Short term I think we'll adjust the test to look for this.
On Windows we mostly run CNIs as Windows services (although we'll be moving them to DaemonSets as HostProcess containers mature) so we should only be seeing terminal failures if the sandbox container does not start.

Long term we'll work with Alex and others to see if we can have runPodSandbox calls can indicate if a failure should cause the Pod to fail and/or be rescheduled on a different not or if the Failure is re-tryable.

/triage accepted

once test is adjusted this needs to be converted to a kind/feature or create a new feature request to work on re-tryable failure
